tools.name: list_available_slots
tools.description: Return the live available start/end pairs for one event type. These are real times on a real calendar: show them to the person and let them choose. Do not invent, extrapolate or round a time that is not in this response. Convert times for display only — pass the original values back to create_bookin

tools.name: list_upcoming_bookings
tools.description: List up to 100 upcoming confirmed bookings. This is the only way to verify that a booking exists. Use it after every create or cancel, and use it first whenever a write returned an uncertain outcome.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "create_booking" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Book a real meeting. This sends invitations and writes to connected calendars, and it cannot be undone except by cancelling. Ask the person to confirm the event…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_event_types, create_booking · Public sink: list_event_types, create_booking.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_event_types, create_booking · Public sink: list_event_types, create_booking

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
